topic.title: Learning under Noise: Statistical and Computational Limits
topic.overview: This cluster studies what can be learned efficiently when labels, observations, or gradients are noisy and the ambient dimension is large. Halfspace and ReLU learning provide central examples where sample complexity and computational complexity can diverge. Sparse approximation, regularization, and concentration bounds supply related tools for controlling estimation error.
topic.whyItMatters: Having enough information in a dataset does not always imply that an efficient algorithm can extract it. Distinguishing statistical limits from computational hardness prevents unrealistic expectations about what better optimization alone can solve.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives analyze sparse regression and regularized consistency. Recent halfspace work compares malicious, random, and Massart noise, producing near-optimal algorithms and hardness results. The newest examples also apply geometric and spectral bounds to transport and low-precision attention, illustrating broader uses of the same quantitative style of analysis.
openQuestions: Which realistic assumptions close information–computation gaps in noisy learning?
Can robust guarantees adapt to unknown noise strength without excessive sample cost?
